page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-16 is a compute-oriented virtual server configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs built upon the arm64 architecture. The platform provisions 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. This reduced memory footprint relative to processing cores designates the system for CPU-intensive operational demands rather than memory-heavy database caches.

Hardware integration is focused purely on core compute capabilities. The instance includes no bundled local storage, meaning operating systems and persistent data rely on external network-attached volumes. In addition, the configuration features zero hardware GPUs and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Standard x86 instruction sets such as AVX and AMX are not present due to the underlying ARM64 processor design.

By omitting local disks and expansive memory overhead, the resource profile prioritizes computational density and execution cost efficiency. The configuration is suited for scalable, compute-bound workloads compiled for ARM64 targets, including CI/CD build agents, batch processing pipelines, web serving fleets, and distributed container microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-16 is a compute-focused instance powered by 16 dedicated vCPUs on an arm64 architecture paired with 32.0 GB of system memory. It includes no bundled local storage and zero GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached block storage for persistence and OS hosting. The instance also provisions no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Due to its dedicated ARM cores and lean memory footprint, this instance provides cost-efficient execution density for CPU-bound tasks. It is well suited for running containerized microservices, software build and continuous integration nodes, batch data transforms, and scalable web serving environments optimized for ARM64 operating environments.
